request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty in the request and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case; a blank value behaves as no value; an unmatched name yields an empty list, not a failure. The page keeps the narrowing while paging.
acceptance_criteria: /vets.html?specialty=<name> lists only the veterinarians holding that specialty, and the page count reflects the narrowed list
a narrowed page's pagination links carry the specialty, so moving to another page keeps the narrowing
/vets?specialty=<name> returns only the veterinarians holding that specialty, unpaged as today
matching is on the whole specialty name, ignoring letter case; a name that is only the beginning of a specialty matches no veterinarian
a veterinarian holding several specialties is listed whenever any one of them is named
a specialty no veterinarian holds yields the normal page or machine-readable document with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200
an empty or whitespace-only specialty behaves as if none had been given, like the empty owner search
without a specialty, both surfaces behave exactly as they did before: the page lists every veterinarian five to a page, the machine-readable form carries them all
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty
free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits
narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
notes: REQ-VET-004 is minted in docs/prd.md for the machine-readable directory, reinstated as a supported surface on the owner's decision; withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. REQ-VET-004 needs no production change - the surface exists - so this slice only guards it with a test. Whitespace handling: the owner tied blank values to 'the empty owner search', so a specialty with surrounding spaces matches the same specialty without them (REQ-OWN-002's rule). The visible-control question is recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions, per the owner's 'may come as a follow-up request'. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new non-goal ADR; that file is owned by the system-design-expert.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing sits entirely inside the vet feature package and reuses the shape the owner search already demonstrates: a declarative Spring Data derived query taking a Pageable, a controller that binds the parameter and selects the call, and a Thymeleaf list template. Two things make this new ground rather than a repeat. First, the vet lookups are cached and the narrowed key space would be caller-supplied and unbounded, so a decision was needed and is recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-database-narrowing-of-the-vet-directory.md: narrow in the database, keep the narrowed lookups out of the vets cache, leave the unnarrowed lookups exactly as they are. Second, architecture-principles.md forbids a new business rule in a web controller and states the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new ones. The rule for reading the parameter - strip surrounding space, treat a blank value as no narrowing - therefore lands in a new immutable value object RequestedSpecialty in the vet package, not inline in VetController as OwnerController does it. Both vet routes read the parameter through it, so the two surfaces cannot drift. docs/system-design.md Contracts now carries REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 on the vet rows, and the Known Defects row claiming the machine-readable route serves no requirement is removed - REQ-VET-004 retires it.
integration_points: /vets.html gains an optional specialty request parameter; absent or blank, the handler takes exactly today's path through the cached paged lookup
/vets gains the same optional parameter; absent or blank, it takes today's cached findAll path, so REQ-VET-004 needs no production change and is guarded by a test only
VetRepository gains two uncached narrowing methods - one returning Page<Vet> with a Pageable, one returning Collection<Vet> - both matching the whole specialty name ignoring case
vetList.html pagination links carry the specialty; the controller adds a specialty model attribute only when the request narrows, so the link builder omits the parameter otherwise
no change to Vet, Specialty, Vets, the schema, or the seed data

patterns.description: derived query taking a Pageable - the shape the two narrowing methods follow; VetRepository extends Repository rather than JpaRepository, so each method is declared explicitly, with @Transactional(readOnly = true) as the neighbouring methods carry
String.strip() plus a blank-means-broadest branch - the same rule RequestedSpecialty encapsulates, but there it sits inline in the controller and here it must not
findPaginated builds the PageRequest with a local page size; the narrowed call reuses it rather than introducing a second page-size declaration
existing pagination links use Thymeleaf expression preprocessing (__${i}__); the specialty must NOT be added that way - see risks

risks.risk: Adding the caller-supplied specialty to the pagination links through Thymeleaf expression preprocessing (__${specialty}__) splices request text into the expression before it is parsed, which is expression injection, and it also skips URL encoding. The existing links use that form for the page number, so copying it is the obvious move.
risks.mitigation: Build every pagination link with link-expression parameters instead: @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes parameter values and omits a null one, which also gives the unnarrowed case its current URLs.

risks.risk: @Cacheable on either new method would key an unbounded cache on caller-supplied text; the vets cache declares no size limit and no expiry.
risks.mitigation: Leave both narrowing methods uncached, per docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-database-narrowing-of-the-vet-directory.md. The pre-existing caller-controlled key on the paged lookup is recorded as open question 5 and in the threat model; it is out of scope here.

risks.risk: The derived name findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase must resolve the nested property through the ManyToMany set; if Spring Data cannot derive it, the query fails at context startup rather than at runtime.
risks.mitigation: Fall back to an explicit parameterized @Query in JPQL, the project's existing exception to fully derived queries. Do not build the query by string concatenation.

risks.risk: Joining the vet-specialty collection can duplicate a vet across the result and distort the page count.
risks.mitigation: An exact match on one name yields at most one join row per veterinarian, so no duplicate arises; the paging test asserts the narrowed total, which catches it if this reasoning is wrong.

risks.risk: Putting the strip and blank-means-absent rule directly in VetController repeats it across two handlers and adds a fresh business rule to a controller, which docs/architecture-principles.md flags as a new violation rather than an extension of the recorded one.
risks.mitigation: RequestedSpecialty holds the rule, is immutable and equal by value, validates at construction, and is unit-tested without the web layer.

notes: Verdict is new rather than minor because the caching decision needed an ADR and the vet package gains its first non-entity type. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: (1) new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-21-uncached-database-narrowing-of-the-vet-directory.md; (2) docs/adr/README.md index rows for that ADR and for the product expert's docs/adr/2026-08-21-non-goal-veterinarian-free-text-search.md, which was missing one; (3) docs/system-design.md - Contracts rows wired to REQ-VET-003 and REQ-VET-004 including a new RequestedSpecialty row, the machine-readable-route Known Defect removed, open question 5 extended with the cache key space, a threat-model row for unbounded cache growth, and the specialty parameter added to the Security Context inputs. Coverage claims rest on reading the vet and owner sources directly, not on an IDE oracle - none is connected in this run. Whitespace: OwnerController uses String.strip(), so RequestedSpecialty.strip() matches REQ-OWN-002's recorded rule the PRD ties this slice to. The visible-control question stays out of scope and is recorded in the PRD's open questions.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: RequestedSpecialty is an immutable, equal-by-value record with the narrowing rule enforced in its compact constructor (Assert.hasText + strip()), matching the naming rule (domain noun, no suffix) and keeping the business rule out of VetController

Both VetController handlers read the parameter through the same RequestedSpecialty.from(), so the two surfaces cannot drift, and findPaginated/findVets stay small, single-responsibility, side-effect-free query helpers using Optional.map/orElseGet instead of imperative branching

VetRepository's two new derived queries follow the existing declarative style (Repository, not JpaRepository; explicit @Transactional(readOnly = true)) and are deliberately left off @Cacheable with javadoc pointing at the governing ADR, avoiding an unbounded cache keyed on caller text

vetList.html builds every pagination link via parameterized link expressions (@{...}(page=...,specialty=...)), never Thymeleaf preprocessing, so no caller-supplied specialty reaches the expression parser; a template comment records why the null-test repeats across all five links, matching the ADR's documented trade-off
./gradlew checkFormat and checkstyleMain both pass clean on the changed sources

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: `RequestedSpecialty.from` applies no length bound, so an arbitrarily long `specialty` value reaches a DB bind parameter on every request, and (by the uncached-narrowing ADR) each distinct value is an uncached query. Harm is bounded by the database and by a baseline that already has no rate limiting, so this is not a regression against the recorded posture - but a maximum-length guard in `RequestedSpecialty` would cap the amplification at the boundary where the rest of the contract already lives.

Supply chain was not verified against the NVD in this review: `build.gradle` configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin (`dependencyCheckAnalyze` is unavailable), and the reviewer has no network access. The change set touches no build file, so the resolved surface is unchanged from the merge base (Spring Boot 4.1.0 via the BOM, `mavenCentral()` over TLS with the nohttp check active). Treat the CVE check as not run rather than clean, and close it in CI or by a human.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the narrowing goes through the Spring Data derived query `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String[, Pageable])` on VetRepository. No JPQL/SQL text is composed from the request parameter anywhere in the change set; the whole-name, case-insensitive match is expressed by the method name, so the caller's text arrives only as a bind parameter.

Cross-site scripting / template-expression injection: every vet pagination link in `src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html` passes the specialty as a link-expression parameter (`@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}`), never as preprocessed expression text. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter and HTML-escapes the attribute, so caller text can neither reach the expression parser nor break out of the href. A grep for `__${` across `src/main/resources/templates/` finds no preprocessing on this page; the surviving instances in `owners/ownersList.html` take integers and template-supplied values only, and this slice adds none. `VetControllerTests.theVetListPaginationLinksShouldEscapeTheRequestedSpecialty` pins the escaping with an attribute-breakout payload. The divergence from the neighbouring owners-list pagination pattern is the safer direction and carries both an inline template comment and an ADR, satisfying the Pattern Consistency clause.

Boundary validation is single-sourced: `RequestedSpecialty.from` is the one reader of the raw parameter for both surfaces, so the HTML and JSON routes cannot drift on what caller text means. Absent, empty, and whitespace-only all narrow nothing; surrounding space is stripped. The record is immutable and the controller holds no per-request mutable state, so the singleton bean stays thread-safe.

Fail-secure error handling: the record's `Assert.hasText` message is a fixed literal and is unreachable from the controller (guarded by `from`), so no caller-supplied text can reach the error page that renders exception messages (system-design.md Known Defects). No new exception message carries request data.

Cache key space: the narrowed lookups are deliberately left off `@Cacheable("vets")`, keeping caller-supplied text out of the unbounded, unevicted `vets` cache. This is the correct call against the pre-existing unbounded-cache-growth threat row and is documented on the repository methods and in the ADR.

No exposed-surface widening beyond the recorded baseline: `/vets` and `/vets.html` already existed and both remain read-only `GET`s. No new endpoint, no management-endpoint change, no new dependency, no binder or mass-assignment surface, no file or resource path composed from request input, no shell execution, no deserialization entry point, no logging of request values, and no secret added anywhere in the diff.

Threat model updated with the change: system-design.md gains a template-expression-injection row for the echoed specialty and extends the cache-growth row to record the narrowing's exclusion, so the durable security memory matches the code that shipped.

findings.description: vetList.html renders five independently-conditioned pagination links (numbered, first, previous, next, last), each choosing between a plain and a specialty-carrying link expression on a null test - the design-block (line 10) calls this five-way repetition a named risk and claims 'the unnarrowed-URL assertion in VetControllerTests catches the regression.' author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty

blast_radius.note: Thirteen files but one module: the whole production change is the vet feature package - a new RequestedSpecialty record, two derived repository methods, both VetController handlers - plus its own vetList.html. No sensitive paths, and six of the thirteen files are docs. The widest reach is the rewrite of all five pagination links in vetList.html, which touches every render of that page including unnarrowed ones, but it is confined to that single template.

semantic_surprise.note: The hunks do what the description says, and the one non-obvious mechanism change is deliberate and pinned: all five pagination links move from Thymeleaf preprocessing to parameterized link expressions chosen on a null test, and tests assert the unnarrowed hrefs come out byte-identical, including page=1 for the first and previous forms at page 2 of 3. The strip-then-validate order in the record compact constructor is safe because the factory guards blank values before construction, and the new specialty model attribute shadows the table body loop variable of the same name only in a disjoint element scope, so it changes nothing today.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behavior rather than restating it: ignore-case, prefix-no-match, multi-specialty and narrowed page counts run against real H2 in ClinicServiceTests, a derived-query semantic no mock could verify; RequestedSpecialtyTests covers null, empty and whitespace values plus the surrounding-space strip; and the MockMvc tests drive real Thymeleaf rendering, including an attribute-breakout payload and both narrowed and unnarrowed backward links at page 2 of 3. build_passed is true across build, test, check, checkFormat and checkstyleMain.

reviewer_hedging.note: Three of four reviewers approved with no findings, but the security approval carries two standing recommendations: RequestedSpecialty applies no length bound, so an arbitrarily long caller value reaches a bind parameter on an uncached query on every request, with amplification bounded only by a baseline that already has no rate limiting; and the supply-chain CVE check was explicitly recorded as not run rather than clean, left for CI or a human to close. The test-reviewer also requested changes in round one on a real pagination-coverage gap, which the fix-delta closed before a clean re-approval.

scope_deviation.note: The change tracks the three recorded owner decisions exactly: a URL contract only with no page control, NG-9 narrowed through a non-goal ADR, and REQ-VET-004 minted for the reinstated machine-readable surface with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn. build_retries is 0 and consultations 0; the single design revision was bookkeeping over uncommitted doc paths plus a corrected Thymeleaf assumption about null link parameters, not a scope move, and the visible-control question was parked in Open Questions rather than built.

rationale: Code and tests read clean: the narrowing is contained to the vet package, unnarrowed URLs are pinned byte-for-byte, and matching semantics are proven against real H2. The residual is the security review's two open recommendations - no length bound on an uncached, caller-keyed query, and an unrun dependency CVE check. Decide both before merging.
